name: inprocess-obi-apb-rational-pair-f1f4
description: One Ibex RVFI OBI CPU at its pinned 50 MHz declaration and one PULP APB3 timer declared at 30 MHz: the pair has no whole half-period divider (50:30 = 5:3), so the entry places both models on the exact common grid of lcm(50,30) = 150000000 Hz.  One grid step is 1/(2 x 150000000) s, the reference CPU half period is 3 grid steps and the target's is 5, and one host tick advances 6 grid steps.  The run states the measured rising-edge counts for both models, so the 50:30 ratio is an observation.  No DMA and no IRQ behavior is declared, so F5/F6 are refused by name.
notes: The 30 MHz profile is a declared composition variant of the pinned PULP apb_timer: same RTL, source revision, reset and APB3 pin contract, only clocks[0].frequency_hz differs.  The pinned profile is not edited; assume_single_clock is absent so the exact rational grid is the only admitted schedule.

lcm(50000000, 30000000) = 150000000: one grid step is 1/(2 x 150000000) s, the reference CPU half period is 150/50 = 3 grid steps, the target's is 150/30 = 5 (exactly 5/3 of a CPU half period), and one host tick advances 6 grid steps.  clock_plan.json states grid_lcm_hz 150000000, grid_steps_per_cpu_half 3, grid_steps_per_tick 6.

The target is slower than the CPU (5 grid steps per half period against 3), so it is sampled once per its own cycle: one rising edge per target cycle and one APB3 trace sample per target cycle.  Its rising-edge count divided by the CPU's is the declared 30/50 ratio; both are printed per case on the clockcase line and in total in the summary.
No behavior file and no DMA profile are declared: this scenario claims only F1-F4, and F5/F6 stay named refusals.
